review: Fourth independent computer-owned chat migration review
disposition: All nine confirmed findings fixed on main; regression and integration checks pass.
scope: Full computer-owned storage feature, legacy migration, recovery, durability, queues, desktop/mobile loading and reconnect integration; not only the latest commit.
provenance: Fixes and integration checks ran in the uncommitted main working tree. Original red-test evidence remains labeled before-fix; unrelated concurrent edits were preserved.

findings.title: Closing a tab during migration can erase uncopied prompts
findings.trigger: Tab A is the original task-content owner. Tab B copies its own history without task-wide prompts. Close A after B activates, before B cleans up.
findings.impact: Cleanup elects B as the new content owner and deletes task-wide prompts that were absent from its verified transfer. The normal service retry succeeds after the data is lost.
findings.proposedFix: Give task-wide content durable migration ownership independent of tab lifetime. Freeze it in the checkpoint, clean only verified copied content, and explicitly migrate any remaining task-wide records.

evidence.test: review: closing the original content leader cannot erase prompts excluded from a sibling transfer
review: normal hub migration and tab close preserve task-wide prompts

findings.implementedFix: Task-wide prompts have their own durable owner. Cleanup deletes only source rows proven present in the verified transfer.

findings.title: Mixed-computer migration creates conflicting session owners
findings.trigger: One task has Claude history recorded on computer 1 and Codex history on computer 2. Both migrate, then both computers reconnect.
findings.impact: Each transfer contains every task provider session. The first recovery claims both sessions; the second fails with Provider conversation belongs to another storage owner.
findings.proposedFix: Separate historical session metadata from exclusive ownership claims. Assign ownership only with deterministic tab/computer provenance, preserving conflict fences and historical records.

evidence.test: review: legacy providers with different recorded computers reconnect without cross-claiming sessions
evidence.failure: Error: promise rejected "Error: Provider conversation belongs to a…" instead of resolving

findings.implementedFix: Historical session metadata no longer claims every provider session. Proven old cross-provider misclaims are repaired; real owner conflicts stay fenced.

findings.title: Switching chat provider leaves the new provider unusable
findings.trigger: Initialize a Claude main chat, switch the main tab to Codex Chat, then open it.
findings.impact: The tab retains its immutable Claude storage binding. Codex hydration fails with Chat tab ownership mismatch; the selected provider cannot open.
findings.proposedFix: Implement an explicit provider/binding transition that fences the previous writer and preserves previous history. Keep strict invocation identity checks.

evidence.test: review: changing main provider preserves history and admits selected codex-chat
evidence.failure: Error: promise rejected "Error: Chat tab ownership mismatch" instead of resolving

findings.implementedFix: Provider changes stop and fence the previous writer, archive its history and queue, and copy the unsent draft to the selected provider. Interrupted changes resume safely.

findings.title: A rejected queued message clears text and attachments
findings.trigger: A turn is running or a queue exists. The computer goes offline; the user submits another message.
findings.impact: The composer clears before remote queue admission succeeds. A rejected admission leaves no input, queue entry or failed-message bubble. Desktop is reproduced; the equivalent mobile path is source-confirmed.
findings.proposedFix: Persist a local pending submission with stable identity before clearing input. On rejection retain or recover text/files without overwriting later edits; handle lost acknowledgements without duplicate delivery.

evidence.test: review: queue submission preserves input until accepted, offline=true
evidence.failure: AssertionError: expected '' to be 'keep unsent queued input' // Object.is equality

findings.implementedFix: Pending sends persist locally before RPC with one stable ID. Failed or ambiguous sends retain text/files; retry cannot duplicate an accepted send or clear newer edits.

findings.title: Typing during the first offline load has no durable draft
findings.trigger: Open a chat whose initial draft read fails while the computer is offline. Type text, then close or reload the tab.
findings.impact: Local journaling waits for the first successful remote read. No local journal or server save exists, so the only draft copy disappears.
findings.proposedFix: Journal edits immediately, including an unresolved server revision. Reconcile safely with the authoritative saved draft when the computer returns; preserve both copies on conflict.

evidence.test: review: typing before an offline draft load must journal the only local copy
evidence.failure: AssertionError: expected null to match object { Object (text) }

findings.implementedFix: Typing is journaled before the first remote read. Owner/revision conflicts preserve both drafts; late saves are fenced and valid unsent copies never expire by age.

findings.title: Retrying a drained message can permanently block its queue
findings.trigger: The original queued message drains, but its acknowledgement is lost. Retry the same client message ID under a fresh operation ID, then enqueue another message.
findings.impact: A duplicate queue row is created. The outbox already knows that message and emits no new user-message event to remove it. The duplicate remains at the head and later messages never reach the provider.
findings.proposedFix: Deduplicate durable message admission/delivery identities across operation IDs and validate payloads. Atomically reconcile already-delivered queue rows without another provider invocation.

evidence.test: review: retrying an already-drained queue message cannot block later messages, newOperation=true

findings.implementedFix: A task-wide, content-free message identity index survives drain, retention, provider changes and tab deletion. Reused IDs cannot start another provider turn.

findings.title: A short computer disconnect leaves the visible chat stale
findings.trigger: The provider finishes while the computer link is down. The renderer remains connected to the hub, and the computer reconnects between availability polls.
findings.impact: The answer is safely stored on the computer, but no replay/invalidation reaches the open chat. Availability is sampled ready before and after, so the shared desktop/mobile hook never reloads history.
findings.proposedFix: Publish an authorized reconnect generation or history watermark and catch up from it independently of sampled availability transitions. Faster polling alone cannot guarantee recovery.

evidence.test: review: computer reconnect maintenance must expose persisted output, dropped=true
review: computer reconnect refreshes missed history, sampledOffline=false
evidence.failure: AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality

findings.implementedFix: A recovery/binding watermark and explicit signal reload missed output even if availability was always ready. Hidden tabs and in-flight status requests catch up safely.

findings.title: A failed purge can delete the only working file copy
findings.trigger: An artifact has external changes not yet saved as a version. Task deletion removes its working file, then a later SQLite write fails or the transaction rolls back.
findings.impact: The task and artifact rows return to an active state, but the unversioned file bytes are already gone. An injected final SQL abort reproduces this rollback window.
findings.proposedFix: Commit the tombstone and a durable filesystem-cleanup intent first. Perform idempotent file removal after commit and resume unfinished cleanup after restart.

evidence.test: review: a failed task purge preserves externally edited working originals with the live DB rows
evidence.failure: AssertionError: rolled-back deletion must preserve the only working original: expected false to be true // Object.is equality

findings.implementedFix: Deletion first commits its tombstone and cleanup intent. File removal happens afterward, with startup and IO-failure retries.

findings.title: Tool metadata can retain expired attachment bytes
findings.trigger: An old user attachment expires, but a retained tool payload contains an object with the same artifactId and contentHash.
findings.impact: Retention recursively treats opaque tool data as an attachment reference. The expired attachment pin and private bytes survive; the control without similarly shaped metadata is collected.
findings.proposedFix: Use the normalized eventAttachmentReferences and recordAttachmentReferences helpers. Inspect real user-content containers rather than arbitrary tool payload objects.

evidence.test: review: opaque tool metadata cannot retain an otherwise expired sealed attachment (metadata=true)
evidence.failure: AssertionError: expected { events: 1, records: +0, …(3) } to match object { events: 1, attachments: 1 }

findings.implementedFix: Retention recognizes normalized user attachment references and ignores attachment-shaped tool input.

passingScenarios: Real migration chain upgrades from schemas 171 (v0.36.2), 177, 182 and 186: mixed Claude, Codex and Gemini history, drafts/prompts, then reconnect: 4 passed.
First bootstrap interruption before request or after a lost acknowledgement, followed by archive/Trash, isolated computer restart and restore: 4 passed.

Positive controls: same-provider hydration, same-operation queue replay, continuous connection, sampled-offline reconnect, previously loaded draft, accepted enqueue, opaque metadata without an attachment-shaped object.
limits: Two private pre-upgrade corpus checks remain skipped: no private database/blob fixture was supplied.
Released-schema fixtures cover the real migration chain; retained-host fixtures restore old contracts in disposable bundle copies, rather than every historical released binary.
Tests use temporary data and fake providers; no live databases, billed providers or physical power-loss test.
Fixes committed on main. The live app was not restarted during this work.
harnessNote: Inherits packages/shared/test-utils/vitest.harness.config.ts, with globalSetup disabled and maxWorkers=1; caller isolation/setup retained. Renderer uses packages/apps/app/vitest.config.ts and excludes **/.claude/worktrees/**.
next: Ship matching hub/computer binaries; older busy hosts finish through the maintenance bridge.
provenanceBeforeFix: Tests ran in the shared working tree. Every cited defect source file matched committed HEAD; unrelated concurrent edits were excluded from findings.
additionalRegressionFixes: Delayed duplicate provider controls cannot stop the replacement session; late binary resolution cannot revive the previous writer.
Old-host contract v1/v2 remains stop-only while busy; v3 replacement restores full readiness without changing enrollment.
Superseded transfer payloads are collected only after activation proves the same ownership lineage.
Same-provider round trips fence stale draft/scroll writes and preserve late acknowledgements without changing newer journals.
Asynchronous local journal writes preserve submission order; local confirmation cleanup failures do not re-send accepted work.
